steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Ah, you're back! I was just about to go find you.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: How come you've got sand stuck to you... did you go to the shore?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I told you not to go! But you just don't listen.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Hurry, come inside with me, it's warm.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Fine. This is for you! I found something to eat. I gave those clothes I half-sewed to Uncle Fireplace, and took some things from his. He's got quite a lot of food left, so he shouldn't mind it.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It'll be forever before winter comes. If I just work at it a little more, I'm sure I'll find materials to use.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This shellmeat...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Just what is it you're eating?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Ow! It hurts when you grab me like that... you're much too strong!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What is it you're eating...?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: We—We pick them off the coast!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: There is no food in the sea here. Nothing to harvest whatsoever. This part of the ocean is silent.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I told you, if you went to the shore today, of course there'd be nothing to eat.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: The time has to come...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What time?

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: One-hundred...

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: One-hundred!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Oh, no! I hadn't even paid attention to the count. We're already at a hundred, then.

a.text: As if receiving some sort of signal, each 'busied' person scattered all across the street assembles together.
From all their mouths the same number comes, as they surround a pot, one after another remove something identical thing from it, and then silently leave.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That pot.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Weren't you asking me where all the food came from?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: On every hundredth flood and ebb of the tide, the grownups all get together like this, and each one takes a shell out from it.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: The shells in the pot are mostly white ones, and only one is red.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Once the sun's gone down, the one who's taken the red one will go to the shore.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: And on morning the next day, there'll be food all over the shore.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: And the one who went?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Went to go live in the sea. Just as the laws say.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You believe in this too?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Well, where else do you think they go?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: One-hundred. It has finally come.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Here, Woodframe, why that face? This is a good day!

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Very soon, out of us, another lucky one will be chosen. They will leave before us, to live a better life.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Come tomorrow, we will even have, fresh food aplenty. We will all survive. No matter whether gone to the sea, or left on the shore.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You do not need to worry. You are already old enough. Very soon you will join this too, and have this greatest, opportunity.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: For now, you may go on as before. Give your blessings to that sibling.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Sheetmetal, I, I...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You have fallen over. Truly hopeless. What happened at the shore, earlier, weakened your leg.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: I do not understand why. I, I am so hungry... I have no strength. I am ill... I am going to die.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: That is right, what about the shell? The one I just drew...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You dropped it on the ground.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Is it... Is it a red one?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: Can, I go to live in the sea?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: In the sea, I will not hunger. Is that not right, Sheetmetal? I will live, a good life.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: You will... erk, bless me too, as the priest told, will you not?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You have mistaken it.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Take it, for this is your shell. Look carefully at, what color it is. Do not let the saltwater muddle your eyes.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: A white one? Why would it be white... did I see wrong? I could not have. My eyes, are very fine.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Plucks strings)

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You are here too.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: So this, is how you use that thing.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant B
steps.text: *cough*, Sheetmetal, the shell in your hand... your hand, is clutched so tight. It is bleeding, is it not? I can see, reddest red...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: If it's blessings you want, I have none for you.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: You understand nothing.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: This is what is truly meaningful. I know, at least, where I should go. I will very soon learn.
What are you all doing?!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: That outfit... it's an Inquisitor!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: What is an Inquisitor doing here all of a sudden? They come so rarely.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It was so many years ago when an Inquisitor last came... I was still very young then, and we were all living miserably.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: We couldn't find any more food in the city, and so many of us were ill. Everything was a mess, and everyday people passed away.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: The Inquisitors took a few people away. Those people never came back.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Since then, the days have gotten a little better. We still starve, or die of illness, but at least we won't, um, we won't...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I mean... that's an Inquisitor.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Shh, singer, don't anger her. She doesn't seem very happy at all.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I've seen what's happening here, and I've even heard it. You're plotting to send someone into the sea... Do you not know what it is you're trying to do?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Speak! Why won't you speak? I don't like it, I don't like anything about this place. Disease, famine... I thought I'd have seen it here, with how hard it is to escape from.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: According to prior reports, none of you should even be alive at this point, after all these years!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Yet reality begs to differ. You all seem to me in better shape than I'd imagined, yet blighted all too fiercely.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Do you all understand what your actions will eventually cause?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Look at me, answer me! Don't you know who I am?

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: You are an Inquisitor.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Thus, you are required to answer me, citizen!

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: This is the ocean's choice. The one who is chosen is the one who accepts it.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: This isn't right! What in the world is the ocean's choice? As if the ocean had some kind of will of its own... a truly unsound suggestion!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: The way I see it, you are conducting a collective murder! How could anyone entering the sea survive? On... on what basis do you sentence the innocent?

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: Entering the sea, is not death.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How do you know?

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: Do you know?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I... That's irrelevant. I only know that their departure will in all likelihood be more terrible than death itself.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: And right now, I witness that you are coercing one amongst you.

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: We are not making them do it. This is their own choice.

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: If they want to go to the shore, we should not obstruct them. The laws do not say they cannot do this.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Unbridled nonsense! This is not in any way proper!

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: Then, what is proper? You are an Inquisitor. You may indicate to us.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: At the very least, I know more about wrong than you all seem to.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What you're carrying out is impermissible conduct. Whether you see it or not, I still smell an odor of wickedness—

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: (Draws sword)

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: It seems you have no fear of my sword. Perhaps, though, you truly don't consider this a homicide.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You fear not even death. You're all becoming monsters before my very eyes.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Or yet... I suppose there's someone who wants you turned into monsters.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: It may be your insanity was tugged astray by some actor. I will unearth this sin's source, I swear!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm out of here.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She's the one who can't hold it in. It's nothing to do with me.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Who... Who's she? Do you mean... the Inquisitor?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Let's at least let her try.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You've looked in an awful lot of houses this whole way.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You don't need to follow me.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Can you really find who you're looking for, turning through one building after another like this?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll keep looking, then.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Traveling the city north to south, west to east, would take a whole day or two.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: If you didn't follow me, I could move faster.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Does the one who wanted you here know you're looking for her? Didn't she mention any specific place?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Ugh, it'll be dark in just a bit, so let's rest up. Singer, have you readied anywhere to stay tonight?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Anywhere will do.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You can head back with me. I've mentioned the buildings in the north are a little better for wear. Plenty of us all live together.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Look, there was still a little fin oil left over from last time. Uncle Fireplace was up early to light the lamps, and now the room's nice and bright.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll be fine.

a.text: Skadi randomly kicks open a roadside door. The door belongs to a half-collapsed building.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll stay in here.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: This one? This one hasn't had anyone in it for forever.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't care about that.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Never mind a bed, you'd barely find a single even nook in there. If you can't lie down, how are you going to sleep?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Standing, sitting. It makes no difference.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Incredible...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You're so strange. I didn't know what wandering singers were like, but the feeling you give me isn't like them.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I thought people who love singing would all love laughing, joking. Not like you, you barely talk.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: And would people who love dancing not mind sitting somewhere dust-caked like you are, getting your skirt all dirty?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You should go home.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Are you annoyed with me now?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This is no good place. As you said.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: But I want to keep you company.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't need company.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Ugh, I realized. You've stared outside the whole time you've been here. Where are you looking at? The shore, the chapel?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Are you going to head out again at night? Say, climb the hill, and take a look inside the chapel?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That is none of your business.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: True, it isn't. I'm just curious.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Take it.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Your harp? What are you giving me this for?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You've been eyeing it the whole time. If you want it, just take it.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: What a pretty harp.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: (Plink-plunk)

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Such a nice sound. But I have no clue what to do with it. I can only watch you use it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Then what do you want?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Do you feel as though I'm only following you because I want what's yours?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I just want to follow you, really.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I know the only thing on your mind is finding someone, finding that fellow one of yours.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I need to verify a few things.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You've been searching for her for many years now, haven't you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: That's the feeling you give me. The moment I mention finding her, the look in your eyes is different. They're the eyes of someone who's been on so very many journeys. There's times when the look in Grandma Petra's eyes is the same.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: So wonderful. I think, in the end, you can free yourself from her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Burdens like this are too heavy.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't understand what you mean.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: No matter how long you persist for, come twenty or thirty years' time, whether it's you or her, you'll only want to be freed.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: And no one can persist for that long of a time, besides.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What are you saying here?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I'm saying, you might just be the kind who's fated exceptionally well. You don't have to search for her anymore.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Here, only those without any burden can live for very long. If their minds are fixated on one thing for so long, they go mad.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Don't take me just for someone young. I've seen a lot of people go mad.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You don't understand.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I don't understand what happened between you in the past. But things of the past, good or bad, can crush people once too much amasses.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Just like I'm unsure if Grandma Petra's illness has gotten worse, every time she brings up the name Manuel.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You're still young. You don't need to live such a hard life.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Things aren't as simple as that.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Simple or not, you can try talking about it all the same.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I'll be right here. I want to hear.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They're...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Even if I don't pay them mind, they won't just leave.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The more I don't pay them mind, the more they'll come find you, drown you...

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Here, you drink some too.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (She tilts her head and gulps.)

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Stop—not too much in one go, leave a drop for me. I need some too to help with sleepless nights.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Goddamn. You piece of work, you.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: My ass, you're the disaster. You got Juan killed... This damnable papá couldn't even give you an earful in time before you came back looking half-dead. What the hell can I even say to you?

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: I can't. A tomar por culo. I can't deal with it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The enemy's aim was me. No one who nears me... has a happy end.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Look at what you're saying. Cursing me, aren't you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You should keep your distance from me too.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: That I can do. Don't have to ask me twice.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: All right, sichtír, that doesn't mean I believe you're some ill omen. This line of work's bloodthirsty, and that little idiot didn't listen to his papá, died, and died in some goddamn mystery asshole's hands. If even you couldn't do anything, did I ever have a chance?

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: That's not a hatred I can avenge. I've got nothing I can do to you either.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Once we're done with this bit of drink, we'll be off again, going wherever we go.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: You bastard! Were you always like this? Can't even find a single kind word, not so much as a profanity, huh?!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I've never been too good at the language here. I'm still not.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Nah. You're just not willing to admit you've made a friend.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Dammit. If we're to part, you might as well spare a couple more words. Where are you heading next?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Same as ever, then. Drifting here and there, taking on missions with no point, fighting wave after wave of enemies who couldn't even take you if you were using one finger. Like living in an unending dream, isn't that?
Skadi tilts back and swigs. But the alcohol seems without a shred of effect on her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Then where can I go, in your opinion?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You're all bounty hunters in order to make money, to live.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: But I long since had nothing left.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's savage, orderless. There's not even an automatic toilet. I don't want to be here, and this place doesn't need me. Why should I be here?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Weak, ignorant. Both plainly insatiable yet scared of dying. The things don't even understand me, yet when they come looking for me, they're not even willing to get out of the way.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I can't figure it out.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Hold it, did you just crush a few bottles?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Beheading prey. Disposing of enemies. I'm born to do this.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They all die, and I live on. What do I live on for? Why do these disasters always come calling, but never kill me... always the ones by my side?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Juan was a good person.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: I don't need you to tell me, you damned Ægir hag!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Then why? Why is it always them who die?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I await, I search, I make sure all those shadows pursuing me will be slain, but I can't even find them, I can't even catch sight of them.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: So what am I meant to do? What can I even do, except keep far away from everyone?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Who can even... tell me at this point?

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Fine, fine. You win. Tah-hathek.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: This whole bottle's yours. Down it, give crying your eyes out a go, like me. Then get some proper sleep.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It doesn't do much. I've already tried.

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Go dream actual dreams, hunter. For you, dreams might just be the more real thing. You never know, maybe you'll find some clues in there—you know, like a, uh, treasure map that only belongs to you?

steps.name: Old José
steps.text: Find it. And then you can be on your way all the better. Cover your head and move forward. It beats being stuck circling in place.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: A treasure map.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer? Are you okay?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You seemed very pained for a moment... I didn't know you could make that sort of face.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: And then you started pinching this thing. If you didn't treasure it so, I would've believed it was some awful artifact that angered you so much you wanted to pulverize it.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You don't... look angry at all.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This is hers.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Her? The fellow person you're looking for? Fine, I can see you just won't give up.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...She's not a burden.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She's the... one who helped me. She revealed the course of a craft to me.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: If I keep following its direction and sailing on, maybe I'll be able to find answers.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, what are you looking for?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I still don't know. It may be who I am. It may be what I should do.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: When... When you're searching for things in the ruins, do you know what you're possibly going to find?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Wow. Put like that, I actually don't know.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I think, once I've found it I'll know.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Let me in!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Shoot.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, don't you cross words with her. Open the door.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You're not an Iberian.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Say what you will.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: That's an Inquisitor. Hmm...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I know you're in there! Don't get cocky about your disguise, I saw you the moment you entered the city!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Open the door, citizen. You don't know what kind of person you're sheltering...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Sheltering? No, I, I didn't mean to hide her...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I'll give you a count of three. If you don't open up, don't blame me for being discourteous.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: One, two—

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Three! *cough*, *cough* *cough*, so much dust! How long has this place been uninhabited...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Aha, Ægir, I've found you!

a.text: The Inquisitor's blade is keen and swift, the air itself practically sundered in two.
The one meant for the blade's downswing turns her waist, sliding to the side in one unfathomable motion.
She keeps close with the blade's point, and it follows her unerringly, yet it cannot split even one of her hairs.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Wh—What fast moves—

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer... did you dodge?! That posture... I can't imagine it myself.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Stood on the chair... the backrest? People can stand on that? How is she stood so steadily?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: A fluke and no more!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I must see for sure, how long can your good luck last you?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She dodged again! In a single swish—she went from this end of the house to that... She's even lighter than seagrass flung in a gale, even faster!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That stick of yours is useless against me.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: St... Stick?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: This is an affront...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You will pay for your false words!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Whoaaa—so strong too! The chair split apart, the cupboard, and now there's even a crack through the floor!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I—I can't bear to watch... oh, the singer...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Wait, she's alright? She evaded all of that? Such nimbleness!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: No... it doesn't seem like she's dodging. Her steps aren't forced in any way. It actually has a peculiar feel of rhythm to it...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: So—So beautiful.

a.text: Sweat drips from the young Inquisitor's flushed face. Her blade hand is still steady, but her breaths are coming faster.
The narrow room is cut to utter pieces. To Skadi, this is no different to her slow ambles across the open barrens.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How long do you plan to hide, Ægir?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Like the rest of your kind, you steal into our country, stowing away in the shadows—

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Heyah!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Did that slant away? The slash cut against the wall...?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Has the Inquisitor... tired out?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Heh! At no moment does my sword ever slant—

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: The—The wall collapsed!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: How fortunate, we're on the other side...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: But the singer... has no way out now. The Inquisitor did that intentionally.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Nowhere left to hide.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Take this blow, for it is your crimes put on trial!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Damn it.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Gh... how?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How can my blade be so casually blocked?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Though I have not used all my strength... person of Ægir, just what are you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: A wandering singer.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Drivel! I've been following you ever since you entered Sal Viento.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Who are you fooling? What wandering singer... has such skills?!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Seems Mister José wasted his effort.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: And who is this José?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: And your acts at the shore! I saw it all!

a.text: The Inquisitor flurries her blade, hacking and slashing, thrusting, each blow coming quicker, more exact than the last.

She no longer simply charges the Ægir in her gaze, but relentlessly switches angles, blitzing slices through the surrounding space. If the enemy shows no openings, her swordhand will force the openings from them.
However, Skadi is open, head to toe. She has no intent of defending at all.
Every supple strike melts, one by one, into a traceless muffle.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Confess! Why have you stolen into our land?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You care too much.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: S—So strong!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She's not just unafraid of the Inquisitor, she's taunting her?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It might not be a taunt. The singer just speaks this way. I've gotten used to it after half the day. But... *cough*, now the Inquisitor is even angrier.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I am an... Inquisitor!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: All things that occur in Iberia are my business.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: All errors proscribed under the law... we find, we even out.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: There's something not right about the sea here. Their numbers have grown. This city is on the eve of... no, perhaps it has already become a lair of evils.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Speak, Ægir. All these abnormalities, they are all your doing, correct?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: It was you who brought about disaster, had those things assemble here—

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You inculcated heretical thought into the citizens here, drove them to enter the sea. Look at them, they've all now become as grotesque as you!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You undoubtedly saw it. You clearly brought something about in the ocean here. Yet see the look in your eyes—

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You simply—do not care!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How can such indifference claim resemblance to a normal human? And you dare to say this wasn't your doing?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I will not let you escape, Ægiii—iiir! Do you consider the calamity you've brought to this country a trifle? Your lot are scheming something, of this I am absolutely certain!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: What's the Inquisitor talking about?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: The singer's only been here for half a day... and what disaster? Who's grotesque?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Don't we... voluntarily enter the sea?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: What other Ægir are there?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I don't understand.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You can't overcome me.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How can we know without trying further?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This is a pure waste of time.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Tch. You're correct. What have I been wasting all this talk on you for?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I should have long since—apprehended you first.

a.text: All of a sudden, the Inquisitor sheathes her blade. From her side she draws a handcannon, grips it in both hands, and aims at Skadi.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Huh?!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Get down. Don't come out.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Heh, do you know my might now, Ægir?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (She brushes off her hem.)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: An extra bullet hole. Can't return this to Mister José in original condition now.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You... You! You're without a scratch?! How could you be? My aim was true!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Are you finished?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Your weapon. You don't use it lightly.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Otherwise, you wouldn't be talking to me now. You ought to aim a second time.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't understand what you're talking about, nor do I care.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't want to...

a.text: A beam of light pierces the dead of night, shone directly on Skadi's face.
At the far end of the road, from where the light came, appears a single figure carrying a lamp.
Skadi's face shows no expression, her impatience just now gone with it.
But in the instant she sees that not-so-bright light, the Inquisitor's face shines.
